title: Spikes on the floor with a certain order.

posts.author: SakuraMiya
posts.body: For my game, I'm making a room that has your typical spikes on the floor. I know that you have to use region ids for the player to take damage, but how can I do it when the spikes move like this?

posts.author: Solar_Flare
SakuraMiya
posts.body:
Solar_Flare said:
I think
not
doing that might work better in this case, actually.
I threw together a quick proof of concept for you in MV.
Set up your event like this:
View attachment 348465
For that script call to work, you'll need the following code in a plugin. If you don't want to use a plugin, you could make an autorun event on the map and put it in a script call, followed by a Control Self Switch A = ON command.
JavaScript:
Game_Interpreter.prototype.checkPlayerHere = function() {
    var ev = $gameMap.event(this.eventId());
    if(!ev) return false;
    return $gamePlayer.x == ev.x && $gamePlayer.y == ev.y;
};
The key points on the left-hand side are the custom move route and the Parallel type. The move route should look like this:
View attachment 348466
You'll probably want to change the wait values both in the move route and the event contents – I set it to 5 for testing, but that's quite slow. If it's best with no wait at all in the move route, you might need to fiddle with the event commands to avoid lag (possibly move the wait into the inner conditional and figure out what value works).
Again, this works in MV, and would probably work in MZ as well. The concept probably works in other makers as well, but the JS code would need to be translated into Ruby.
Click to expand...

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: You could try removing the wait in the event contents. I think that might cause some other problems (in my testing, spikes are getting out of sync with each other when offscreen), but it should make it trigger every time the spikes are up.

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
you could have also had one parallel event increment a variable, use a modulus so that its values can ever only be 1-5, and then set each of those events as player touch with page conditions for each being specific variable values.
you wouldnt need to check the pattern or set up movement routes. youd just have 2 pages where the default is that the spikes are down and an active page where theyre up

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I don't think that works without a plugin? You can only check if a variable is
greater than or equal to
a specified value, but for this use-case you need to check
exactly equal to
. It would probably work with something like HIME_CustomPageConditions though… but I'm not sure how the two intermediate frames of the animation would fit in with that model. (The original poster appears to have chosen not to use them, but personally I would prefer to use them.)

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
the loop of the 4 rows,  the top 3 (start in middle has those wait.
30, 45  // row 1
25, 40 // row 2
20, 35 // row 3
15, 55 // row 4
5, 50 // row 5
numbers are wait, so you have a move route of 30 wait, same moveroute
below it, but with 45 wait in between, 4/5 frames per turning (down/left/right/up)
and back down.
so you have the effect like:  1,2,3,4,5,3,4,5,1,2,3,4,5,3,4,5 in repeat session.

I had forgotten that touch events arent triggered when the event is activated while a player is already on them, so the activated spike pages are parallel and just check if the player is on them. it didnt need script, but its easier for me to type that than to event it

$gamePlayer.x === $gameMap.event(this.eventId()).x && $gamePlayer.y === $gameMap.event(this.eventId()).y
Switches could have also been used instead of variables, but depending on how many possibilities of active spikes there should be it might take a bit more to set up.
